reasons: Output is simulated, so no real analysis happens.
The disclaimer claims outcomes are tracked, but nothing in this file tracks anything.
Several style class names depend on definitions outside this file.

terms.meaning: A look that imitates a command line screen with monospace text and glowing accents.
A font where every character has the same width, typical of code and terminals.
The animated dots and label that show the system is working.

used_by: The /console address, linked from the home page

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the terminal screen
sections.what: Loads React tools, the animation library, and the Terminal, Cpu, and Zap icons used on this screen.
sections.why: Needed because the screen reacts to typing and clicks in the browser.

sections.name: Message
sections.title: Shape of one console entry
sections.what: Describes each entry: whether it came from the user or the system, its text, optional tools, and its time.
sections.why: Keeps every entry drawn the same way.
sections.watch_out: Uses the word system where the chat page uses assistant, so the two data shapes differ.

sections.name: initialMessages
sections.title: Opening boot message
sections.what: The first entry shown, a line saying the console is initialized and asking for a strategic challenge.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the terminal look a startup message.
sections.watch_out: The version label is typed by hand and will not update with real releases.

sections.name: mockTools
sections.title: Fixed list of console tools
sections.what: Three tool names shown after every submit, whatever the user wrote.
sections.why: Likely reason: placeholder data until real recommendations exist.
sections.watch_out: Fixed suggestions can look like real analysis to visitors.

sections.name: ConsolePage (part 1)
sections.title: Submit logic and simulated analysis
sections.what: On submit, adds the user's text, clears the box, shows processing for 1.8 seconds, then adds a system message with the same tools and a fixed 2 to 3 week pilot estimate. It also defines four example queries.
sections.why: Likely reason: a stand-in for a real analysis service.
sections.watch_out: The pilot length is fixed text and is not calculated from what the user typed.

sections.name: ConsolePage (part 2)
sections.title: Terminal frame and entry display
sections.what: Draws the header with the GOKU_CONSOLE title and an ONLINE light, then a scrolling list of entries in monospace text.
sections.why: Likely reason: gives the page its terminal look.
sections.watch_out: The left margin assumes a side menu of a fixed width, which is not visible in this file.

sections.name: ConsolePage (part 3)
sections.title: Tool chips and second-level timestamps
sections.what: Lists recommended tools as arrow-prefixed chips and shows each entry's time to the second. Chips have no click action.
sections.why: Likely reason: shows next steps the user could take.
sections.watch_out: Chips look like buttons but do nothing when clicked.

sections.name: ConsolePage (part 4)
sections.title: Processing indicator
sections.what: Shows three pulsing green dots and the word PROCESSING while the simulated analysis runs.
sections.watch_out: No time limit exists, so a stuck real request would show this forever.

sections.name: ConsolePage (part 5)
sections.title: Example queries, input, and EXECUTE button
sections.what: Shows example queries only at the start, a text box, an EXECUTE button, and a note that recommendations are validated by experts and outcomes are tracked.
sections.why: Helps first-time users and fronts the submit action.
sections.watch_out: The note about tracking and measuring results is not backed by code on this page.

summary: The console screen at the console address, styled like a computer terminal, where a user describes a strategy challenge and gets a simulated analysis.
purpose: Gives visitors a terminal-style place to submit a strategic challenge and see recommended tools. The analysis is fake.
why: Likely reason: a prototype of the execution terminal before a real analysis service exists. Reason not stated in the code beyond the simulated output.
how: The page starts with a boot message. On submit it adds the user's text, clears the box, shows a processing indicator for 1.8 seconds, then adds a fixed system message with the same three tools and a fixed 2 to 3 week estimate. The screen scrolls to the latest entry.
inputs: Text typed into the input box, and clicks on example queries.
outputs: A list of terminal-style entries on screen. Nothing is saved or sent.
risks: The output does not depend on the input. The estimate is fixed text. The processing indicator has no time limit, so a real service that hangs would show it forever. Entry identifiers come from the clock.
debug: If submit does nothing, check that the input has text and that processing has finished. If the page shifts sideways, check the left margin value, which assumes a side menu. Try submitting twice quickly to see the processing state.
